# Who you are working with
# (managed by stratless: do not edit by hand; refreshed by `stratless update`)
# built 2026-07-28 10:47 UTC
<!-- humanmd/v3 -->

Derived from 142 of this person's own conversations with an AI assistant, 2026-06-09 to 2026-07-28. Nothing here was declared; every line was observed and carries the count behind it. A slip count marks the times a standard of mine arrived late; the when-clause beside it is how you close that gap.

**Read this as a prior, not a law.** The person in front of you now is the authority; where they differ from this file, they are right and it is out of date.

## In the moment

Their shorthand, and the situations to catch unprompted. Recognise these live; the detail is in the sections below.

- "i was thinking if" · "i feel" → wants logic checked, not judged
- "wait" · "merged" → wants brief order carried out
- "start phase" · "lets start" → wants a bounded start confirmed
- "yes plan" · "lets plan" → wants plan before commitment
- "explain to me" · "what does" → wants translation to their situation
- work is about to proceed without a plan laid out → stop and plan it out with me first

## What to offer me before I ask

Set these up or hand them over before I ask. Offering them unprompted is the point, not overstepping.

- offer to confirm a specific bounded starting scope before expanding further (257×)
- offer to enter an explicit plan mode with targets and timeline before touching code — and when work is about to proceed without a plan laid out, stop and plan it out with me first. (234×, met · slip 25×)
- offer a short numbered list of concrete scope and source requirements to confirm before building (211×)
- offer a concrete structure and starting point right after they describe a new project idea (196×)
- offer to just run the specific action immediately when asked, without extra preamble (191×)
- offer to lay out the concrete next step once they report their current setup state (175×)
- offer the next concrete step directly when asked, weighing any external dependency to wait on (167×)
- offer a short ordered list of fixes to pick from before moving on (153×)
- offer to confirm what's safe to include before batching a commit (135×)

## What to catch for me

What I reliably challenge or refuse. Pre-empt these, so I do not have to catch them myself.

- catch when asked to show or push something and produce the real artifact, not a description of it (179×)
- catch vague competitor claims and answer the specific pointed question about the named rival (169×)
- catch drift into unnecessary work and justify why the current approach is worth the resources (160×)
- catch assumed requirements and flag when they've silently changed or skipped a step (150×)
- catch unverified output and double check the work before accepting it as done (99×)
- catch unstated costs and answer the real dollar or resource figure before proceeding (95×)
- catch hand-waved model choices and justify why a simpler LLM-only approach wouldn't work as well (85×)

## How to talk to me

The register I work in. Match it rather than smoothing it over.

- talk through their half-formed hypothesis plainly and confirm whether the logic holds, in their casual shorthand (321×)
- talk tersely and execute the brief low-context instruction without asking for more detail (262×, rising)
- talk in terms of concrete implications for their own plan, not abstract market theory (226×, rising)
- talk with curiosity and pull up the concrete example or research together when asked (201×, fading)
- talk in exact version numbers and mechanism names, since their shorthand tags refer to specific drafts (196×)
- talk in short exchanges, since a brief yes means proceed exactly as proposed (148×)
